card.name: Attan
card.era: Ancient; possible Zoroastrian/pre-Islamic roots, codified over centuries
card.tagline: Afghanistan's whirling circle dance, drum-driven and proudly national
card.profile: Attan is the national dance of Afghanistan, originating among Pashtun tribes of southern and eastern Afghanistan and northwestern Pakistan. Dancers form a circle around a dohol (double-headed barrel drum) player, beginning with slow steps that accelerate, with spins, hand-claps, head and hair flicks, and handkerchiefs; a performance can last 5 to 30 minutes (Wikipedia; Britannica). Once danced by warriors before battle, it now features at weddings, engagements and Nowruz; regional styles include Kabuli, Logari, Paktia/Khosti, Wardaki, Kandahari and Herati.
card.insight: Britannica notes the open-air Attan "became the national dance of the Pashtun and then of the entire country," and it was banned under the Taliban; Afghanistan has applied to UNESCO to register it (Arab News), making it a potent emblem of Afghan identity, though it has not yet been inscribed.
